name: Bolgo
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 5 other works consulted do not discuss stress.

MA thesis, University of North Dakota, Grand Forks. xiii+156 pp. (UND Theses and Dissertations 2869,https://commons.und.edu/theses/2869). Convergent: Kastenholz, Raimund. 2017. La langue bolgo du Guéra (Tchad): Notes de recherche et matériel lexical. Arbeitspapiere des Instituts für Ethnologie und Afrikastudien der Johannes Gutenberg-Universität Mainz 172. 48 pp.
catalog_locator: Tikka 2019 §2.4 Tone, pp. 44-45; also §3.2 Tone in nouns p. 49 and §4.3 Tone in verbs pp. 92-93; Kastenholz 2017 §2.1.3 Ton, p. 8.
catalog_quote: In our data, we found high (H), mid (M), and low (L) register tones (or level tones). ... Thus, Bolgo also follows the most common tendency in Bua languages by having three tone heights. I also found certain examples of falling or contour tones in the data, but these are not phonemically contrastive (see section 3.2). ... Regardless whether a syllable is monomoraic or bimoraic, it may never bear more than a single (level) tone. Any surface contours in Bolgo are due to the phonetic realizations of one of the level tones, and are not underlying. This indicates that the tone-bearing unit in Bolgo is the syllable rather than the mora. ... While there are minimal pairs for tone, they are not extremely numerous, and thus the functional load of lexical tone is not very high.
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.locator: §2.4 Tone, pp. 44-45 (PDF pages 58-59); see also §3.2 Tone in nouns p. 49 and §4.3 Tone in verbs p. 92
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (170 PDF pages, text present, title page: 'Phonology and morphology of Bolgo.. University of North Dakota.. Master of Arts, Grand Forks, North Dakota, December 2019'; BA UW-Madison 2013 -- so the compilers correction of Glottolog's 'school = University of Wisconsin-Madison' is right). Printed pp. 44-45 = pp. 58-59, section '2.4 Tone': every sentence of the quoted passage is there verbatim; the [..] gaps are where the quote skips intervening sentences (Yip 2002 / Boyeldieu 1986 discussion, the grammatical-tone paragraph, the orthography paragraph). Section 3.2 'Tone in nouns' (p. 49, PDF 63) and 4.3 (p. 92, PDF 106) also confirmed. Surrounding chapter 2 covers consonants, vowels/ATR,…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Bolgo is described as a register-tone language with three level tones (H, M, L) on every syllable; the syllable is the tone-bearing unit, phonetic contours are not contrastive, and lexical tone has a low functional load. Neither Tikka 2019 nor Kastenholz 2017 (§2.1.3 Ton, p. 8: 'le bolgo a un sytème tonal de trois niveaux distinctifs, haut (H), moyen (M) et bas (B)') says anything about word stress or accent — no stress position is stated and stress is not mentioned at all.
new_statements.exceptions: None regarding stress. Tikka notes grammatical tone in the verb system was not investigated (p. 45); monosyllabic verbs show only L and M (p. 92); Kastenholz notes tone marking in his material is incomplete and, for pronouns, 'très peu fiable' (fn. 18).
new_statements.domain_note: Lexical (word-level) tone established from a tone-sorting exercise on monomorphemic noun and verb roots elicited in isolation (Tikka p. 44); Kastenholz's data are wordlist citation forms. Convergent statement in Boyeldieu et al. 2018 §4.4 (HAL p. 12): 'Ɓa, Lua, Tun, and Bolgo have tone systems with three contrastive heights (Low, Mid, and High)'.
new_statements.identity_note: Tikka 2019 describes the Bolgo Dugag dialect (endonym Tɛɾɛw; Glottolog bolg1253), with side data from Bolgo Kubar and Koke; Kastenholz 2017 describes Bolgo Kubar, subgroup Bólgò / 'Bolgo de Kodko' (Glottolog bolg1252). Both agree on a three-height tone system. Note Glottolog gives Tikka's school as University of Wisconsin-Madison; the thesis title page and UND repository record say University of North Dakota (Grand Forks), MA thesis, Dec 2019 (her BA was UW-Madison 2013).

tone_statements.quote: Il nous semble assez évident que le bolgo a un sytème tonal de trois niveaux distinctifs, haut (H), moyen (M) et bas (B). Dans les cas où un mot/une entité lexicale n'est pas marquée pour le ton dans le matériel présenté ici, le ou les ton(s) lexicale(s) n'ont pas pu être établi(s) par l'auteur. Une syllabe peut apparemment être liée à plus d'un tonème; comparer les cas suivants: [...] Les deux derniers exemples démontrent, d'une part, que dans certains cas seulement, une accumulation de tonèmes résultant d'une élision d'unités porteuses de tons est à la base des tons complexes
tone_statements.translation: It seems fairly evident to us that Bolgo has a tone system of three distinctive levels, high (H), mid (M) and low (B). Where a word/lexical item is not tone-marked in the material presented here, the lexical tone(s) could not be established by the author. A syllable can apparently be linked to more than one toneme; compare the following cases: [...] The last two examples show, on the one hand, that only in certain cases an accumulation of tonemes resulting from elision of tone-bearing units underlies the complex tones
tone_statements.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
tone_statements.n_tones: 3 levels (H, M, L) plus complex/contour combinations on single syllables

tone.says: Full text (copy) §2.4 Tone pp. 44-45: three register (level) tones H, M, L established by a tone-sorting exercise on monomorphemic noun and verb roots; surface falling/contour tones exist but are not contrastive; a syllable never bears more than one level tone, so the TBU is the syllable; grammatical tone (TAM) reported for Bua by Boyeldieu but not investigated for Bolgo; §3.2 tone patterns in nouns pp. 49-52, §4.3 tone in verbs pp. 92-93.
